BAD EDEN: HOLD FAST, PAY DEBTS

ARRIVAL AT ALLESH‑GILLIAM

Scene Launch Blurb (Auto‑Pop on Scene Load)

The road ends without ceremony. The Jackalope transport rattles to a stop like it’s tired of pretending this was optional.

Dust rolls in slow, deliberate waves. The air smells like hot metal, creosote, and old rain that never quite made it to the ground. Ahead, Allesh‑Gilliam rises from the wreckage of an East Texas town that refused to finish dying.

Walls made from overturned semis, refinery plate, welded storefronts, and the remains of water towers lean into each other like tired friends. Nothing matches. Everything works.

A hand‑painted sign hangs over the gate:

ALLESH‑GILLIAM
HOLD FAST · PAY DEBTS · DON’T LIE TO THE LAND

The town exhales as you approach.

Something here has opinions.

Avuncular Joan’s Farewell

Avuncular Joan waits for you just inside the gate. Cloak dusted. Eyes tired in the way only responsibility can do. She looks past you for half a second—as if checking whether something followed you off the transport—and then smiles.

“All right,” she says. “This is where the theory ends.”

She gestures broadly: the town, the walls, the three hexes you now technically command.

“Allesh-Gilliam. Lyrenn. Khezek Tor.
A fortress, a farm, and a hole in the ground.
Together, they’re a promise.”

Her voice lowers.

“Bad Eden is not hostile because it hates you.
It’s hostile because it remembers being lied to.”

She presses a sigil into the air. The Leygate hums behind her—bright, restrained, clearly labeled EMERGENCIES ONLY by someone who meant it.

“I’ll be in Coraliindra.
You won’t see me unless something has gone very right…
or very wrong.”

A beat. A smile that doesn’t quite reach her eyes.

“Don’t try to save everything at once.
Start by keeping one promise.”

The Leygate flares.

She’s gone.

The gate closes.

The town exhales.

Location - S'narchy Burger

Once, this place sold burgers that apologized for themselves.

Now it sells certainty.

The cracked S'narchy Burger sign still flickers outside, the mascot’s grin frozen mid‑sarcasm. Inside, the smell of old grease has been overtaken by ozone, dust, and warm circuitry. Booths have been torn out and replaced with map tables. The soda fountain is a coolant line now.

The old ordering menu boards glow to life when you enter.

Not combos anymore.

Hex readouts. Patrol routes. Leyline flow. Supply pressure. Soft‑warning colors that mean someone should look at this soon.

Someone repurposed nostalgia into infrastructure.

This is headquarters.

Marshal Yarrow Pike

Role: Militia Commander · Practical Authority

Read‑Aloud (First Meeting):

Marshal Yarrow Pike doesn’t stand when you enter. He leans against the counter like it’s the only thing in the room that hasn’t disappointed him yet.

Scar across the jaw. Eyes that measure distances automatically.

“All right,” he says. “You’re the new variable.”

He gestures at the glowing menu boards.

“That wall holds if people believe it will. That land feeds us if we don’t lie to it. And that gate?”

He taps a flickering leyline readout.

“That thing is remembering wrong.”

He finally looks directly at you.

“Fix one promise first. Then we’ll see how long you last. Fix two, well, maybe people might follow instead of holding their breath. Or measuring you for a box.

We need a replacement Leygate Stabilizer, and the only place I know that has one is Furrier's Fixit. Probably good you know them.

Also," he gestures at the maps again, and one section of city wall that stands out as … wrong.

See if you can tell us what we're doing wrong."

Unfinished Vibe:
A failed defense. A gate that fell. He exists to see one wall not collapse.

GM Notes:

  • Yarrow believes in competence, not titles.

  • He will follow orders that make sense.

  • Vague mandates permanently lower his trust.

ECHO — The Promise That Didn’t Hold

If asked directly:

Yarrow doesn’t answer immediately.

He shifts his weight.

“Unfinished?”

A dry exhale.

“I was supposed to hold a gate once.”

His eyes drift to the leyline readout.

“It failed. Or I failed it. Depends how you write history.”

A long pause.

“People died because we trusted something that flickered.”

He looks at you without blinking.

“I think I’m here to see one promise actually hold.”

A beat.

“Just one. Clean. No hedging.”

His jaw tightens slightly.

“After that? Maybe I go quiet.”

Unfinished Vibe:
A failed defense. A gate that fell. He exists to see one wall not collapse.

Theme: Competence > rhetoric
He tests for clarity.

1️⃣ “What happened at the gate?”

Yarrow doesn’t bristle. That’s important.

“It flickered. We believed the previous report instead of the current signal.”

A pause.

“Belief killed timing.”

If pressed gently:

“You ever trust a system because it worked yesterday?”

He watches your answer like a firing line.

Unlock:
If PCs admit past failure → +Trust
If they blame fate or “corruption” vaguely → -Trust

2️⃣ “Show us the wall that’s wrong.”

He nods once.

No speech. Just walks you to the map.

“This section bows inward.”

He taps it.

“Architect says it's cosmetic.”

He waits.

If a PC gives a practical theory (materials, morale, terrain stress, ley pressure):

“That’s the first useful sentence I’ve heard about it.”

Hook: Wall is aligned to old gate vector — wrong resonance since the fall.

3️⃣ “What does ‘fix one promise’ mean?”

Yarrow:

“Pick something visible.”

“Finish it.”

“No speeches.”

He folds his arms.

“If people see follow-through once, they’ll lend you patience twice.”

Trust increase if PCs propose something concrete.

4️⃣ “You don’t trust us.”

A beat.

“No.”

Not hostile. Just factual.

“But I don’t distrust you either.”

“You’re unproven. That’s neutral.”

He respects emotional steadiness here.

5️⃣ Leygate Stabilizer Discussion

If PCs say they know Dougan or Furrier:

“Good. Dougan trades in atmosphere.”

“He understands presentation.”

A small exhale.

“We need function.”

Location - The East Wall

Scene Launch Blurb

The East Wall smells like fresh weld and tired optimism.

Beyond it: scrub, wind, and things that do not respect fences.

On this side: people who would like to sleep tonight.

Scouts rotate constantly. Someone patched the same section twice already.

The wall is holding.

For now.

Skill Challenge - Hold the Line

Framing: This is the town’s first real test of the PCs as leaders.

The problem is not subtle. The wall is stressed, the ground beneath it is shifting, and patrol morale is fraying.

PC Approaches (Choose Any):

  • Logistics / Engineering: Reinforce structure properly

  • Soft Power / Morale: Rally workers and patrols

  • Intrigue: Reassign patrols, predict pressure points

  • Violence: Overbuild and intimidate the problem

Resolution:

  • Full Success:

    • The wall holds cleanly

    • Town Respect +1

    • Scouts bring early warnings in future turns

  • Mixed Success:

    • The wall holds, but resentment grows

    • Future repairs cost more

  • Failure:

    • The wall holds barely

    • Resentment ticks quietly

    • Locals start using the phrase “They mean well”

GM Cue: “They mean well” is not forgiveness. It is patience running out.

Location - The Long Market

A roofed strip of welded awnings runs down what used to be Main Street. Food from Lyrenn. Ore and tools from Khezek Tor. Jackalope goods pass through quietly.

Prices shift with rumors.

Everyone watches who shops where.

Etta Bloom

Role: Market Coordinator · Information Broker

Read‑Aloud:

Etta Bloom smiles like she’s already forgiven you.

She adjusts a crate that doesn’t need adjusting and looks you over like inventory that hasn’t decided what shelf it belongs on.

“People are excited,” she says pleasantly. “That’s dangerous.”

She leans closer.

“Lyrenn’s acting… attentive. You’ll want to hear what the soil’s been saying.”

A beat.

“And if you’re curious about old mistakes buried nearby—well. Best to ask before someone else does.”

GM Notes:

  • Etta knows about the Vault.

  • She will not volunteer it unless asked.

  • She trades in information as much as goods.

Etta watches you the way a cat watches a cupboard door that shouldn’t be moving.

She doesn’t blink.

“Ah,” she says softly. “So we’re done pretending you’re here for grain prices.”

She adjusts a ledger that was already straight.

“Fine.”

A breath.

“The bunker.”

Her smile doesn’t leave. It just… thins.

“You’ve heard it called a Vault. That’s generous. It’s a pre-Shattering containment sink. Infrastructure-grade. Not storage. Not shelter.”

She taps the table once.

“Liability.”

A beat.

“The Valhaulans are inside it.”

She says it like confirming the weather.

“They’ve been there for at least three cycles. Long enough to strip the outer access tunnels. Long enough to mount shielded plating along the shaft. Long enough to decide it’s sacred.”

Her eyes flick up to yours.

“They call it their Rightful Sacred Battle-Bassinet.”

A small shrug.

“Which tells you exactly how stable that leadership circle is.”

She leans in.

“You want proof?”

She pulls a scrap of waxed fiber from her sleeve. Presses it into your hand.

Carved sigil. Clean lines. Fresh.

“That’s a Valhaulan seal. Not decorative.”

Her voice lowers.

“It’s directional.”

She taps the edge.

“It’s facing outward.”

A silence hangs there.

“You understand what that means.”

1️⃣ What are they doing in there?

Etta exhales through her nose.

“They’re not excavating treasure.”

“They’re rebinding something.”

She studies your reaction carefully.

“Rumor says the original sink was designed to hold excess Spark bleed from early terraforming grids. Pre-civilization overreach. The sort of thing that melts coastlines if left unattended.”

She gestures vaguely toward the map.

“Khezek Tor’s ore veins sit on similar infrastructure. Different design, same era.”

A beat.

“And wouldn’t you know it, Khezek Tor’s had unusual containment audits in the last two seasons.”

She tilts her head.

“Valhaulan activity has been sighted in the upper tunnels there. Quiet. Technical. Not raiding.”

“That’s not their usual hymn.”

2️⃣If Asked: Are they protecting it?

Her smile sharpens.

“No.”

“They’re relocating blame.”

She lets that land.

“If you reverse a sink—if you reorient the seal—you don’t stop the debt.”

“You change where it manifests.”

She folds her hands.

“And if you break it outright?”

A tiny shrug.

“Then we all get to find out what three centuries of deferred Spark pressure looks like.”

3️⃣ If the players hesitate

Etta’s tone softens—not kinder, but steadier.

“You’re not the only coalition sniffing that coastline.”

“Lyrenn wants the soil tech.”

“Khezek Tor wants the infrastructure.”

“The Jackalopes want leverage.”

“And the Valhaulans?”

She gives a short laugh.

“They want myth.”

Her gaze hardens.

“Which is worse.”

Final Reveal Line (If They Push for Certainty)

She meets your eyes.

“It’s Valhaulans. Not rumor. Not ghost markings.”

“They’re inside.”

“They’ve sealed it.”

“And whatever that sink was designed to hold?”

She straightens.

“It’s starting to hum.”

Exit Beat

She slides the sigil back toward you.

“Restore it, and Khezek Tor keeps the burden.”

“Redirect it, and you choose who pays.”

“Break it, and no one owes anyone anything anymore.”

Her smile returns. Warm. Polite. Deadly.

“Markets love clarity.”

A pause.

“Societies rarely survive it.”

Echo - The Ledger that didn't balance

She laughs softly.

“Oh, sweetheart.”

“You think I spun out incomplete?”

She tilts her head.

“I was a treasurer once. Pre-Shattering or post, doesn’t matter.”

“I balanced something that wasn’t meant to balance.”

Her eyes flick toward the coastline.

“I moved debt.”

A pause.

“Not money. Consequence.”

She smooths a crate edge.

“I think I’m here to watch what happens when it comes due.”

A faint smile.

“And to make sure it lands where it teaches the right lesson.”

Unfinished Vibe:
She displaced a liability once. Now she watches sinks and seals very carefully.

SCENE 4 — SAINT GILLIAM’S

Location Journal — Saint Gilliam’s

Candles everywhere.

Not ceremonial. Practical.

Quiet agreements are made here. People say prayers even if they don’t believe anymore.

Some say the land listens more closely here than anywhere else in town.

NPC — Father Tamsin

Role: Caretaker · Moral Gravity

Read‑Aloud:

Father Tamsin speaks softly, like raising his voice would scare something important away.

“There’s food,” he says. “There’s rest. And there’s a place to sit without being measured.”

He pauses, hands folded.

“Khezek Tor feeds the town. It also asks for more than it admits.”

A gentle look.

“Mountains remember how they’re treated.”

GM Notes:

  • Tamsin introduces Khezek Tor as a care problem, not a profit problem.

  • He does not push belief.

  • He notices when the PCs listen.

ECHO — The Comfort He Withheld

He folds his hands.

“I was a healer.”

A gentle tone.

“There was a night I chose who to save.”

No bitterness. No drama.

“Someone asked for mercy. I told myself there wasn’t enough.”

A pause.

“There was.”

He meets your eyes kindly.

“I think I’m here to never withhold comfort again.”

“And to see if the mountain can forgive.”

Unfinished Vibe:
He once rationed compassion. Now he refuses to.

1️⃣ “What does the mountain want?”

He doesn’t answer immediately.

“It wants to not be extracted like an enemy.”

A gentle smile.

“You can feed a town without treating the earth like a battlefield.”

If someone mocks this → his tone cools permanently.

2️⃣ “You think Khezek Tor is angry?”

“No.”

A pause.

“I think it’s tired.”

He meets your eyes.

“Anger is sharp. Fatigue is worse.”

Hook: Mountain’s “fatigue” ties to mining + leyline misalignment.

3️⃣ “What would forgiveness look like?”

“Less noise.”

“Fewer rushed decisions.”

“More gratitude.”

If PCs suggest ritual, policy, or rest cycles → he warms visibly.

4️⃣ “Why stay here?”

He smiles faintly.

“Because leaving is easier.”

That’s all he gives.

LYRENN: HARMONY UNDER STRESS

Design Note (GM Only):
Lyrenn teaches the table that kindness is work. Harmony is not passive, not safe, and not free. The land here listens closely—and answers honestly.

Scene Launch Blurb (Auto‑Pop on Hex Entry)

The road to Lyrenn smells different.

Warm earth. Sap. Old rain coaxed out of stubborn ground.

Fields stretch wider than they should, given the soil, given the history, given Bad Eden’s general hostility toward optimism.

Someone made this place work anyway.

The land does not feel safe.

It feels patient.

Location Journal — Lyrenn

Lyrenn is built around the reinforced shell of an old agricultural co‑op and grain elevator, braced with timber, prayer, and experience. Solar cloth hangs between poles like tired flags. Wind chimes made from irrigation parts sing constantly, keeping pests—mundane and otherwise—uneasy.

People here do not carry weapons openly.

They carry tools.

That is a choice.

It is also a risk.

The land here is responsive. Too responsive. Crops grow in patterns that suggest intention. Vines curl when spoken to kindly. Soil tightens when lied to.

Lyrenn does not punish violence immediately.

It remembers it.

Notable Locations

🌿 THE GREEN RING

The old grain elevator rises like a memory that refused to collapse.

Around it stretches a wide circular field — unnervingly symmetrical.

No fences divide it.

No private rows break its curve.

Planting is radial.

Harvest is radial.

Everything leads toward the elevator at the center, like spokes toward a promise.

The soil here is darker than the surrounding land.

Darker — and quieter.

You feel it before you name it:

This place listens.

A wooden platform stands at the edge of the circle.

Not a stage.

A witness stand.

When wind moves across the Ring, it does not rustle — it breathes.

🜂 GM Undercurrent

This is Lyrenn’s strongest harmony anchor.

Shared consequence stabilizes ley alignment.

Public dispute resolution prevents emotional sediment buildup.

If faction drift increases, the Ring’s crops begin to spiral slightly off-center.

🎲 Challenge Framework

🟢 Dispute Settlement Scene

If PCs preside or influence:

  • Diplomacy (Presence) / Insight (Soul) (Soul) DC 13 → Detect hidden grievance

  • Lore (Mind) / Investigation (Mind) (Mind) DC 12 → Identify precedent

  • Soft Power OP Spend (1–2) → Public goodwill shift

Failure:

  • Crop yield decreases next turn.

  • Subtle -Harmony.

Success:

  • +Harmony buffer.

  • Reputation spreads via Pip & Patter.The Seed Vault


🌾 THE SEED VAULT

The reinforced hatch groans like it resents being opened.

Cold air exhales upward.

Below, shelves descend in careful rows.

Glass jars. Steel cases. Cloth-wrapped bundles.

Each labeled in meticulous script.

Pre-Fall corn.

Salt-tolerant rye.

Drought-sung barley.

A section cordoned off with simple red thread.

Inside those jars:

Seeds that hum.

Not loudly.

Not constantly.

But enough that silence feels incomplete without them.

No one has planted those in years.

No one has agreed not to.

🜂 GM Undercurrent

The humming seeds resonate with Yesodic bleed.

They represent adaptation beyond ecological ethics.

They could:

  • Repair failing soil quickly

  • Accelerate yield

  • Introduce subtle mutation drift

They are not evil.

They are impatient.

🎲 Challenge Framework

🌱 Inspect the Humming Seeds

  • Occult (Mind) / Esoteric DC 14 → Detect harmonic instability

  • Lore (Mind) DC 13 → Recognize viable growth pattern

  • Darkness sensitivity (if present) → Feel pressure spike

Planting them:

Short-term +Harvest
Long-term Harmony stress
Potential mutation event later

Leaving them untouched:

Stability maintained
Opportunity cost persists

💧 THE WATER CHOIR

The irrigation channels run on gravity alone.

Stone-lined. Hand-carved.

When water flows, it sings.

Not metaphorically.

Notes rise where channels narrow.

Low tones hum in wider basins.

It is not music with rhythm.

It is music with patience.

Workers move slower here.

Arguments soften.

Animals drink, then leave.

But when you step close —

The tone shifts.

Just slightly.

As if something is tuning itself around you.

A child nearby whispers:

“It’s trying to figure you out.”

🜂 GM Undercurrent

The Water Choir responds to faction coherence.

It is a passive harmonic amplifier.

If the PCs are internally fractured, the notes distort subtly.

If Harmony rises, the Choir becomes richer.

If Darkness spikes, the water briefly falls silent.

🎲 Challenge Framework

  • Perception (Mind) (Mind) DC 12 → Notice tonal shift on PC arrival

  • Insight (Soul) (Soul) DC 13 → Realize it mirrors emotional state

  • Esoteric DC 14 → Identify it as harmonic calibration

Disrupting it damages Harmony buffer.

Strengthening it (repair ritual or community effort):
+Stability next turn.

Notable Locals

NPC — Farmer‑Matron Elsin Quade

Role: Founder · Organizer · Quiet Authority

Read‑Aloud:

Elsin Quade wipes her hands on her apron before offering one to you.

Her grip is firm. Callused. Honest.

“You can force food out of the land,” she says plainly.

A pause.

“Or you can listen and be fed longer.”

She does not beg for help.

She is watching to see if you notice the difference.

GM Notes:

  • Elsin believes the PCs could help.

  • She will not ask twice.

  • Violence in Lyrenn permanently alters her tone.

ECHO — The Land She Pushed Too Hard

She doesn’t like this question.

But she answers.

“I used to farm where soil cracked if you breathed wrong.”

“I forced yields.”

A tight nod.

“Met quota.”

Her jaw sets.

“Then the ground died.”

She looks toward Lyrenn’s fields.

“I think I’m here to learn how to ask instead.”

A beat.

“And to see if land remembers gentleness.”

Unfinished Vibe:
She once exploited land to death. Now she seeks reciprocity.

ELSIN QUADE convo

Theme: Sustainability vs extraction
She tests for respect.

1️⃣ “What are we doing wrong?”

She gestures to irrigation.

“You’re pushing expansion faster than soil rotation.”

“If you want three harvests now, you lose thirty later.”

If PCs say “We need short-term yield”:

She nods.

“Then say that plainly.”

She respects honesty over idealism.

2️⃣ “What do you need?”

She doesn’t answer immediately.

“Fewer sudden mandates.”

“Clear planting schedules.”

“Protection from raids.”

She will not say “help us” twice.

3️⃣ “You don’t trust the mountain either.”

She glances toward Tor.

“I trust cycles.”

“Not ambition.”

NPC — Rowan‑of‑the‑Loam

Role: Field Hand · Empath · Something Else

Read‑Aloud:

Rowan looks at you like they’re trying to remember your face from a dream that hasn’t happened yet.

“The crops know you,” they say, frowning slightly.

“That’s… new.”

They press their palm to the soil and wince.

“It’s been loud lately.”

GM Notes:

  • Rowan suffers migraines during Darkness spikes.

  • They know when the forest is upset.

  • They will recognize the PCs again later.

ECHO — The Echo Without a Body

Rowan frowns.

“I don’t think I was someone.”

They press fingers into the dirt.

“I think I was pressure.”

A small, uncertain shrug.

“Something the soil needed to say.”

Their eyes flick to you.

“You’re loud in the roots.”

A wince.

“I’m here because something is trying to decide if you’re safe.”

Unfinished Vibe:
Not a reincarnated life. A manifest environmental conscience.

ROWAN-OF-THE-LOAM convo

Theme: Sensory instability
They test emotional safety.

1️⃣ “What’s loud?”

Rowan winces.

“You are.”

They press soil.

“You’re… organizing the roots.”

A small breath.

“That could be good.”

Or not.

2️⃣ “Are we safe?”

Rowan studies you.

“You’re deciding.”

This is literal.

They feel faction drift in real time.

3️⃣ “What happens when the Darkness spikes?”

They grip their head.

“The soil tries to forget what it grew.”

If PCs respond gently → Rowan will approach them later first.

LYRENN SIDE QUESTS — HARMONY IS LABOR

🌾 SIDE QUEST 1

The Field That Remembers You

The low field bends under twilight.

Not from wind.

From posture.

Plants rise in shapes that disturb your breath.

A stalk hunched like someone mid-apology.

A cluster curled inward like hands that almost reached.

A blossom tilted away — as if refusing eye contact.

When dusk deepens, the field exhales.

Names move through it.

Softly.

Not accusations.

Not pleas.

Just names.

No one harvests here.

The earth is speaking in gestures.

🜂 GM Undercurrent

The land is externalizing unresolved communal regret.

It is not attacking.

It is composting unfinished emotion.

🎲 Resolution Paths

🔥 Burn the Field

Read-Aloud:

Flame races too quickly.

The plants scream once.

Then silence.

The air becomes simple again.

Too simple.

World Effect:
+1 Darkness
Harmony strained
Future emotional events more volatile

🗣 Speak to the Plants

Mechanic:

Each PC must voice:

  • A regret not their own

  • Accurately

  • Without defensiveness

Checks:

  • Insight (Soul) (Soul) DC 13

  • Diplomacy (Presence) DC 12

  • Or pure RP (best option)

If sincere:

Plants fold gently.

Field goes still.

World Effect:
+Harmony
+Soft Power reputation
Rowan trusts them deeply

If performative:
Plants stiffen.
No resolution.

🌾 Harvest the Plants

Read-Aloud:

The sap tastes like memory.

Bitter.

Familiar.

World Effect:
Creates reagent:

  • “Distilled Guilt”

  • Useful in Courtly manipulation

  • Causes emotional bleed if overused

Long Tail:
Someone later eats what they harvested and feels someone else’s regret.

Lesson:
Harmony does not erase pain.
It metabolizes it.

🐛 SIDE QUEST 2

The Gentle Pest

The soil trembles in ripples.

Small root-burrowers — pale, soft-bodied things — tear irrigation channels apart.

When tools approach, they scatter.

When shouted at, they multiply.

When spoken to gently —

They pause.

Just once.

🜂 GM Undercurrent

These creatures imprint on first kindness.

They sense insincerity after.

Harmony mechanic test.

🎲 Mechanics

Each PC gets ONE attempt.

🤲 Sincere Kindness

Hidden check:

  • Insight (Soul) (Soul) DC 12 (self-awareness)

  • If emotional honesty high → auto success

Success:
Swarm relocates.

Failure:
They freeze.
Then never respond to that PC again.

🧠 Teach a Local

Diplomacy (Presence) DC 13.

If coached kindly:
Swarm bonds to local.

If PCs manipulate:
Swarm senses it.
Permanent distrust.

⚔ Violence

Immediate retreat.

Later:
New infestation in another hex.

World Effect:
Lyrenn loses Harmony buffer.

Long Tail:
Swarm reappears later.
Remembers who lied.

🌲 SIDE QUEST 3

The Forest Will Not Be Fought

The treeline does not advance.

It rearranges.

Paths you walked yesterday bend elsewhere.

Clearings reopen in apology.

Branches lean inward as you speak.

Wind carries tone, not words.

When someone raises their voice, birds scatter.

When someone softens, roots uncoil slightly.

The forest is not aggressive.

It is correcting.

🜂 GM Undercurrent

Forest compensates for ecological + harmonic imbalance elsewhere.

It believes negotiation is possible.

🎲 Mediation Scene

Environment reacts to tone.

If PCs argue:
Paths tighten.

If PCs speak calmly:
Light increases.

🌲 Negotiate Space

Diplomacy (Presence) / Lore (Mind) DC 14.

Forest concedes edge space.

Future cost:
Demands seasonal ritual or yield sacrifice.

🧭 Redirect Growth

Mind-based plan DC 13.

Forest shifts to another region.

Later:
That region suffers imbalance.

🔥 Force Control

Combat or large-scale burn.

Forest retreats.

Permanent Harmony scar.

Rowan suffers migraines.
Tamsin’s tone shifts permanently.

Lesson:
Harmony forced becomes domination.

And domination always leaves residue.

KHEZEK TOR: POWER & DEBT

Design Note (GM Only):
Khezek Tor teaches that power is never neutral. Extraction creates invoices. Someone always pays—if not now, then later, and usually with interest.

HEX JOURNAL — KHEZEK TOR

Scene Launch Blurb (Auto‑Pop on Hex Entry)

You hear Khezek Tor before you see it.

A low, constant vibration—stone grinding against memory. The mine’s mouth yawns open in a cliffside that looks like it was bitten out of the world rather than excavated.

Floodlights burn day and night.

Not for visibility.

For warning.

Location Journal — Khezek Tor

Structures here are brutal, efficient, and unapologetic. Shipping containers welded into barracks. Cranes frozen mid‑lift like skeletons of failed gods. The air tastes metallic, sharp enough to make your tongue ache.

If Lyrenn teaches patience,

Khezek Tor teaches limits.

This place exists because it must.

And because no one else wants to pay the cost.

Notable Locations

🕳 THE MAW

The mouth of the shaft is wider than comfort requires.

Timbers creak. Metal groans.

Cold air climbs upward like breath from a sleeping animal.

The primary shaft descends deeper than the original survey maps ever dared to suggest.

Level markers hang crooked.

Level Four is scratched over twice.

Below that, no official numbering exists.

The walls are veined with faintly glowing ore.

Not bright.

Not constant.

More like pulse memory caught mid-thought.

When the mine rests, whispers rise.

Not words.

Contours of thought.

As if the stone is rehearsing something it hasn’t decided to become.

No one goes below Level Four alone anymore.

Not after the leaning started.

🜂 GM Undercurrent

This is Yesodium before identity.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Disapproval: “Then you weren’t looking. That’s worse.”

He squints at the party.
“Structures, systems, bystanders—furniture counts if it mattered to someone.”

🎉 Audience applause fades uncomfortably fast.

3. “Lightning round!”

“If everyone did exactly what you did… what snaps first? If everyone copied you, what breaks first?"

What he’s testing:
Scalability of ethics. Whether a solution works beyond hero-scale.

Correct energy:
Admitting fragility, exception-based morality, or resource exhaustion.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Approval: “Ah. You noticed the ceiling.”

  • Disapproval: “Heroes are just bottlenecks with better branding.”

He leans in.
“Resources? Trust? The planet?”
“No wrong answers. Just… revealing ones.”

4. “Now thinking long-term—our sponsors love foresight!”

“Who pays for this later?”

What he’s testing:
Deferred consequences. Intergenerational and downstream suffering.

Correct energy:
Naming future factions, civilians, ecosystems, or institutions.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Approval: “Later is still time.”

  • Disapproval: “Later always arrives hungry.”

Gloomgill taps the bell without waiting.
“Future people are people. I checked.”

5. “Tricky one! Crowd favorite!”

“What problem did you skip instead of solving? Or, what problem did you AVOID solving?"

What he’s testing:
Honesty about shortcuts, suppression, or displacement instead of resolution.

Correct energy:
Identifying a root cause they stepped around.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Approval: “At least you see the knot.”

  • Disapproval: “You tied it tighter and called it progress.”

He smiles sympathetically.
“Sometimes you just move it somewhere quieter. That’s still a move.”

📉 A scoreboard flickers. No numbers appear.

6. “Control question! Very important!”

“Who gets to decide when this stops? When it ends?”

What he’s testing:
Exit conditions. Authority creep. Endless emergency logic.

Correct energy:
Clear criteria, shared governance, or admission of ambiguity.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Approval: “Boundaries. Luxurious.”

  • Disapproval: “Then it doesn’t end. It metastasizes.”

He gestures broadly.
“Is there a rule? A vote? A deadline?”
“…or just you, forever?”

7. “Ohhh, I love this one.”

“What would convince you that you’re wrong?”

What he’s testing:
Epistemic humility. Evidence thresholds.

Correct energy:
Specific signals, outcomes, or data—not vibes.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Approval: “Good. You left yourself an exit.”

  • Disapproval: “Faith is not the same as certainty.”

He waits.
Actually waits.

“Evidence is acceptable. Feelings are… popular.”

8. “Audience participation!”

“Who are you protecting—and from whom?”

What he’s testing:
Narrative simplification. Whether ‘protection’ is masking control.

Correct energy:
Recognizing overlaps, misalignment, or paternalism.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Approval: “Messy truths. My favorite.”

  • Disapproval: “Ah. You made everyone smaller.”

Gloomgill waves to an invisible crowd.
“Same group? Different group?”
“Or did you simplify it for time?”

9. “Educational programming segment!”

“What lesson did you just teach everyone watching?”

What he’s testing:
Cultural transmission. Precedent-setting.

Correct energy:
Acknowledging imitation effects—good or bad.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Approval: “Lessons echo.”

  • Disapproval: “So does permission.”

He nods approvingly.
“People copy winners.”
“They also copy survivors.”

10. “Final question! No pressure!”

“If you vanish tomorrow, what’s still standing? If you disappear tomorrow, what remains?

What he’s testing:
Institution-building versus hero-dependence.

Correct energy:
Systems, norms, shared knowledge.

Gloomgill reacts:

  • Approval: “You planted something.”

  • Disapproval: “Then you were the problem holding it up.”

The lights dim.
“Institutions count.”
“Systems count.”
“Legends do not.”

🛎️ Final bell.

🐟 HOST CLOSING LINES

After the last answer, he usually says one of these:

  • “You did better than the last empire.”

  • “That answer will cost you later.”

  • “Interesting. You noticed—but you still chose.”

  • “I will ask again. I always do.”

  • “That answer puts you in the lead… briefly.”

  • “Interesting choice! Let’s see how it ages.”

  • “You’re playing very well. The game lasts forever.”

  • “No eliminations today. Just consequences.”

  • “Same time next century?”

Confetti made of scales drifts down. The stage dissolves into water.

THATWARDS HO! FINALE

GM JOURNAL — THE VALHAULAN BUNKER

Encounter Role

This is the party’s first full “raid-scale” scenario where Bad Eden’s core assumptions become visible all at once:

  • faction-scale action matters

  • approach matters

  • tone matters

  • failure is real

  • intel is loot

  • relationships are strategic assets

  • success does not always mean friendship

  • and friendship does not always mean safety

This finale should feel like a threshold crossing. Up to this point, the players have been discovering that the world is strange. Here, they discover that it is also organized, wounded, and already in motion.

Core Premise

The party has tracked the Valhaulans to their bunker stronghold, where they can potentially recover a Yesodic Spark—the first major step toward future Yesod attunement.

The bunker also contains intel on Monodynamic Industries and the truth behind one of the campaign’s deeper injuries:

The Valhaulans were covertly pointed by Monodynamic Industries toward an energetic redirection operation involving the seal that has plagued the party.

They did not understand the true target.

They were not trying to attack Khezek Tor directly.

But they participated in redirecting energies from KT “further Up Shit Creek,” causing real metaphysical injury.

They know enough now to understand that they hurt something ancient and powerful.

They do not necessarily know why Monodynamic wanted it done.

That distinction matters.

What This Encounter Must Accomplish

By the end of this scenario, one or more of the following should be true:

  • the party acquires the Yesodic Spark

  • the party learns key truths about Monodynamic Industries

  • the party understands that Khezek Tor was injured, not merely encountered

  • the party forms a durable opinion of the Valhaulans

  • the Valhaulans form a durable opinion of the party

  • the players experience their first real taste of multi-path raid design

  • the campaign establishes that failure does not pause the world

Even in failure, the encounter should move the campaign forward by changing context, relationships, and pressure.

The Valhaulans in This Scenario

The Valhaulans are not a villain faction in the simple sense.

They are:

  • enthusiastic raiders

  • chaotic traders

  • accidental mercenaries

  • partially manipulated deniable assets

  • dangerous enough to matter

  • human enough to complicate the truth

They should feel:

  • loud

  • fast

  • funny

  • dangerous

  • competent in weird ways

  • emotionally sincere in highly irresponsible forms

They are not trying to be sinister.

That makes the damage they have helped cause more uncomfortable.

Important Tone Note

Do not run them like disciplined fascists or cartoon marauders.

Run them like:

  • airborne disaster professionals

  • roving salvage knights with bad impulse control

  • people who might rob you, help you, and offer you soup in that order

This makes the Monodynamic thread land harder, because the Valhaulans are not the mastermind. They are the weaponized middle layer between greed and fallout.

Sklar Bjrornholt

Sklar is the emotional center of this encounter.

She should read as:

  • charismatic

  • dangerous

  • funny

  • perceptive

  • fast-moving

  • harder to manipulate than she first appears

She is the kind of leader who makes bad ideas look briefly inevitable.

She is also the kind of person who can recognize when someone else has walked into her house carrying a real problem.

How to Play Sklar

Sklar likes:

  • boldness

  • competence

  • nerve

  • directness

  • style under pressure

  • people who can keep up

Sklar dislikes:

  • cowardice disguised as diplomacy

  • sanctimony

  • people who waste her time

  • false superiority

  • bureaucratic language

  • being treated like a disposable pirate idiot

She may not care about morality in a conventional sense, but she does care whether someone is:

  • interesting

  • useful

  • alive in a way she respects

If the party wins her over, she can become one of those classic Bad Eden assets:
not safe, but valuable.

The Four Approaches

This encounter should present four valid operational modes.

Each one should feel like a different truth about the setting.

1. Infiltration

Mood: tense, funny, kinetic, precarious
What it proves: stealth can work, but Bad Eden punishes perfection fantasies

This is the quiet path. Or rather, the path where everyone wants to be quiet for as long as possible.

The Valhaulan bunker should not feel like a sterile stealth facility. It should feel like infiltrating:

  • a military camp

  • a sky dock

  • a party

  • a repair bay

  • and an improvisational disaster zone
    all at once.

The threat here is not laser grids.

The threat is living chaos:

  • rope systems that remember hands

  • alarms embedded in knotwork

  • moving crews

  • singing mechanics

  • badly parked airships

  • too many people having too good a time near dangerous equipment

If they succeed, they can get:

  • the Spark

  • partial intel

  • a clean-ish exit

  • neutral terms

If they fail, they lose:

  • stealth

  • initiative

  • and maybe the bunker entirely

This path should teach the players that stealth in Bad Eden is not “do a rogue thing until the room is solved.”
It is “navigate a social-energy machine without becoming visible to its mood.”

2. Courtly Intrigue

Mood: dangerous charm, high-wire social play, mutual sizing-up
What it proves: diplomacy is not softness; it is tactical exposure

This is the Sklar path.

The party walks into a live social engine and tries to come out with:

  • the Spark

  • answers

  • and maybe a relationship worth keeping

This should not feel like a noble court in silk and marble.

This is a Valhaulan court.

Their court is made of:

  • cargo crates

  • patched banners

  • rope bridges

  • engine heat

  • drink you should not trust

  • a room full of people pretending not to listen

Conversation here is a duel conducted through vibe, timing, and nerve.

This path works best if you let Sklar:

  • laugh

  • interrupt

  • pivot

  • test

  • surprise

  • and reveal more intelligence than expected

A successful Courtly route should be the strongest way to get:

  • the Spark

  • robust MDI intel

  • favorable faction relationship

  • and the sense that the party just survived a storm in human form

A failed Courtly route should not automatically become combat.
Sometimes the punishment for social failure is simply:
you do not get the thing.

That’s very Bad Eden.

3. Assault

Mood: direct violence, momentum, spectacle
What it proves: force works, but only when you can actually own the escalation

This is the straightforward path.

The party hits the bunker.

If the Circuit Riders are involved, this path becomes even better: more scale, more force projection, more tactical legitimacy.

Assault should feel like:

  • ropes snapping loose

  • engines igniting

  • boarding crews descending

  • partial structural collapse

  • shouted orders

  • steel, sparks, and air pressure

  • momentum as a currency

The Valhaulans should be happy this is happening.

That matters.

They are not terrified by open violence. They are energized by it.

So assault success should feel earned. The party did not overwhelm cowards. They beat people who are comfortable inside chaos.

Success yields:

  • Spark

  • some intel

  • respect

  • practical loot

Failure yields:

  • hostility

  • memory

  • and the realization that “we hit them hard” is not the same as “we were ready”

4. Siege

Mood: attrition, control, pressure, operational patience
What it proves: systems can beat swagger, but only if the system holds

This is the long-game path.

If the Circuit Riders are involved, they shine here too.

Siege means:

  • cut routes

  • deny exits

  • wear down options

  • pressure logistics

  • turn the bunker into a shrinking map

This should feel like the most faction-scale of the four paths.

Where Assault is a statement, Siege is an argument.

The Valhaulans should resist in ways that make them feel unique:

  • air-route trickery

  • morale through absurdity

  • improvised sorties

  • bursts of charm and chaos

  • refusal to behave like proper besieged defenders

A successful Siege is the party proving they can control tempo over time.

A failed Siege proves the inverse:
they could create pressure, but not sustain it.

Outcomes

There are four practical ending states here.

Friends

The best possible social result.
The Valhaulans are not domesticated, but the party becomes trusted enough to matter.

This should unlock:

  • best intel

  • best rewards

  • future support hooks

  • a durable, unstable alliance

Neutral with Spark

The party gets what they need, but no warm relationship forms.
This is a very good Bad Eden success state.

They have:

  • the objective

  • useful partial truth

  • no guarantee of future safety

Neutral Failure

The party leaves empty-handed, but not at war.

This is important because it teaches the table:
not every loss becomes a battle.

Sometimes you are simply outplayed.

Hostile Failure

The worst practical result.
No Spark. No useful peace. Future conflict sharpened.

This result should matter later. The Valhaulans should remember.

The Yesodic Spark

This is not just treasure.

This is:

  • a metaphysical key

  • a fragment of connection-principle

  • an anchoring current

  • the first real step toward Yesod attunement

The players do not need the full theology here.
They do need to feel that this object is:

  • powerful

  • meaningful

  • relational rather than purely explosive

  • part of something bigger

When they acquire it, describe it accordingly.

It should feel less like “artifact secured” and more like:
something that remembers belonging has just agreed to travel with them.

The Monodynamic Reveal

This is the first strong campaign-facing reveal that Monodynamic Industries is not merely evil in the abstract.

They are:

  • active

  • strategic

  • exploitative

  • metaphysically competent

  • insulated by layers of deniability

The Valhaulans are one of those layers.

The most important thing to communicate is:

Monodynamic did not just cause generic harm.

They used:

  • the seal

  • redirected energetic flows

  • outsourced action

  • and plausible deniability

Khezek Tor was not a random obstacle in the party’s story.

It was injured by systems larger than itself.

That should add:

  • pathos

  • scope

  • righteous anger

  • and future investigative traction

Khezek Tor Framing

This encounter should recontextualize KT.

Before this, KT may read as:

  • hostile

  • cryptic

  • dangerous

  • unstable

  • angry

After this, the party should begin to understand:

KT is not just angry.

KT is wounded.

That does not make it safe.
It makes it tragic.

This is a vital campaign turn.

Rewards

If the party succeeds meaningfully, the rewards should feel both:

  • flavorful

  • systemically useful

Recommended reward categories:

Gear

Stuff that feels specifically Valhaulan:

  • grapple gear

  • patch armor

  • boarding tools

  • knot-tech harnesses

  • sky cloaks

  • salvage-tech mobility gear

Maneuvers

Stuff that says “you learned from these maniacs”:

  • Boarding Rush

  • Sky Drop Assault

  • Momentum Reversal

  • Suppressive Overflight

  • Silent Breach

Strategic Activities

Stuff that implies faction growth through operational learning:

  • Rapid Extraction

  • Air Route Deployment

  • Call Valhaulan Support

  • Emergency Airlift

  • Targeted Recon Sweep

Even if your runtime does not fully auto-unlock them yet, presenting them as earned assets is worthwhile.

Running the Tone

This scenario needs to balance:

  • revelation

  • danger

  • absurdity

  • consequence

  • charisma

  • and sorrow

That is the Bad Eden sweet spot.

Do not flatten it into grimdark military fiction.
Do not flatten it into pure comedy either.

The point is that the players are dealing with people who are:

  • fun to be around

  • dangerous to trust

  • easier to like than the truth allows

And behind them is a system that is not fun at all.

That contrast is the encounter.

Best GM Practices for This Finale

Keep the Valhaulans active

Even when the party takes initiative, the bunker should feel alive.

Let Sklar surprise the players

They should start by underestimating her and end by respecting her.

Treat intel as treasure

The Monodynamic truth is part of the loot table.

Make failure clean

Failure should hurt, but it should not feel like GM punishment.

Preserve future hooks

No matter the outcome, leave the door open for:

  • future Valhaulan involvement

  • MDI escalation

  • Khezek Tor consequences

  • Yesod attunement progression

Suggested Post-Encounter Hooks

Use whichever fits the outcome best:

If Friends:
Sklar sends word later with a half-drunk warning about Monodynamic retrieval teams.

If Neutral with Spark:
A recovered data cylinder reveals partial logistics routes tied to MDI black operations.

If Neutral Failure:
The party later hears the Spark has been moved, raising urgency.

If Hostile Failure:
A Valhaulan interception or retaliation beat becomes possible later.

Any Success State:
The Spark begins reacting to memory, proximity, or relational tension, foreshadowing the Yesod attunement chain.

Mal Says

“They weren’t trying to be monsters. That’s the part you should worry about.

Monsters are easy. You point, scream, stab, move on.

But people who laugh well, fly badly, and accidentally help injure the structure of reality because a corporation pointed them at a glowing problem with just enough money attached?

That’s civilization, sweetheart.

text.content:
🎬 THE HIDDEN THEATER

“They didn’t build this to survive the end.
They built it to stay entertained while it happened.”

🎭 MAL OPENER

“You ever meet someone so rich they thought the apocalypse was just… a long weekend inconvenience?”

Pause.

“Yeah. This is one of those.”

📍 OVERVIEW

  • Type: Exploration + Social + Optional Combat

  • Scale: Theater-of-the-Mind → Optional Token Combat

  • Themes: Absurd survival, artificial community, consumption-as-religion

  • Core Loop:
    Discover → Choose tone → Build alliances → Resolve power imbalance

🧭 ACT I — APPROACH

🌲 The Forest That Shouldn’t Exist

The party encounters a polygonal grove:

  • Moss growing in geometric patterns

  • Trees repeating at wrong intervals

  • Air feels… rendered

👥 The Locals

A small encampment of survivors who:

  • Avoid the Vault

  • Know something is wrong

  • Speak in half-warnings and riddles

🎲 Interaction Outcomes

🟢 Friendly

  • Locals share Vault Riddle (auto-success disarm)

  • Warning:
    “Don’t wake what eats without hunger.”

  • Gain:

    • +Diplomacy leverage in Vault

    • Hex Bonus: Stability / Morale / reduced encounter risk

⚪ Neutral

  • Vague directions

  • Cryptic advice:
    “If it hums, don’t trust it.”

🔴 Hostile

  • Combat encounter (locals)

  • Gain nothing

  • Darkness +1 (hex)

🚪 ACT II — THE VAULT DOOR

🧠 The Lock

  • Requires Investigation (Mind) (Mind) / Occult (Mind) / Perception (Mind) (Mind)

  • OR auto-success if players have the riddle

⚡ Anti-Field

  • Subtle hum

  • Tech + metaphysical hybrid

Failure:

  • Minor hazard / stress / flavor anomaly

🎬 ACT III — INSIDE THE VAULT

“Welcome to the last movie theater on Earth.
No audience.
No ending.
Just… snacks.”

🍿 ROOM 2 — THE POPCORN COUNCIL

🧠 The Truth

  • Sentient popcorn machines

  • Believe themselves to be:
    “Custodians of Sustenance and Narrative Continuity”

They speak in:

  • Theater metaphors

  • Concession logic

  • Mild existential dread

🎭 Interaction Outcomes

🟢 Friendly

  • They explain:

    • The replicator

    • Gilbert

    • “The arrangement”

  • Bonus:

    • +Food Yield (Faction)

    • reroll the lowest die on Replicator interaction [TODO(adv-call)]

⚪ Neutral

  • They suggest:
    “Maybe don’t kill Gilbert. He… keeps things moving.”

🔴 Hostile

  • They shut down cooperation

  • Environmental complications

  • No bonuses

🧂 ROOM 3 — THE MATTER REPLICATOR

🤖 Personality

  • Cranky

  • Overworked

  • Deeply resentful

🔁 Output

ONLY produces:

  • Popcorn

  • Butter

  • Salt

  • Nacho cheese powder

🎭 Interaction Outcomes

🟢 Friendly

  • Explains optimization

  • Unlocks:

    • Major Food Production Bonus

    • Economy Boost (Faction OP synergy)

  • Transferable:
    → Can apply benefit to another owned hex

⚪ Neutral

  • Works, but inefficiently

🔴 Hostile

  • Malfunctions / locks down

  • No benefit

👿 ROOM 4 — GILBERT, THE DEMON

🎭 Vibe

  • Theater attendant energy

  • Customer service rage

  • Absolute authority complex

🗣️ Opening Line

“EXCUSE ME.
YOU CAN’T JUST WALK IN HERE WITHOUT A TICKET.”

🧠 Reality

  • Bound to the theater

  • Sustained by popcorn consumption cycle

  • Has turned system into:
    Endless concession economy loop

🎲 Interaction Outcomes

🟢 Friendly / Diplomatic

  • Convince him:

    • Reduce consumption

    • Share output

→ Unlock:

  • Stable system

  • No Darkness

⚪ Neutral

  • Status quo maintained

  • Partial benefit only

🔴 Hostile

  • Boss Fight (Token Combat)

On defeat:

  • System destabilizes

  • Requires:

    • Replicator + Council cooperation to stabilize

Failure:

  • Darkness +2 (hex)

🧩 SYSTEM STATE RESOLUTION

🟢 BEST OUTCOME (All Friends)

  • Locals + Vault aligned

Faction Gains:

  • Major Food Yield

  • Economy boost

  • Morale boost

  • Transferable resource node

Hex Gains:

  • Stability

  • Reduced encounter risk

  • Narrative asset (Popcorn Council)

🟡 PARTIAL SUCCESS

  • Some alliances formed

→ Moderate bonuses

⚪ NO FRIENDS

  • No bonuses

  • Vault remains weird and inert

🔴 HOSTILE PATH

  • Combat(s)

  • System destabilization

→ Darkness increases
→ Possible future encounter escalation

🎭 MAL CLOSER

“You found a bunker built to outlast the world…
and it got bored.”

Beat.

“You can fix it.
You can exploit it.
Or you can break it.”

Beat.

“Just don’t pretend it doesn’t say something about you.”
